title: Ask-why cannot find a card by its Jira key or inbox ref in a later session
impact_why: the runner names cards by DOW-3 / DW-3 after the session; nothing maps those to an fp
instrument: memory-cli.test.mjs case: show resolves fp, inbox ref and issue key (0 of 2 non-fp cases today)
evidence:
skill/SKILL.md:448: "use the card list printed in this session. In a later session, ask the runner which card they"
skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:266: "if (!card) throw new DowserError(`proposal ${fp} does not exist`, 2, { error: 'not-found', fp });"
skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:293: "`SELECT fp, lens, status, title, decided_at FROM proposals ..."
body:
## Summary
SKILL.md section 10 tells the agent to ask the runner which card they mean "by its title or its Jira link", but `show` takes only an fp and `list` neither returns nor filters `external_ref` / `issue_ref`.

## Description
`show` (`skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:373-381`) throws on anything but a stored fp; `memory.list` (`skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:282`) selects `fp, lens, status, title, decided_at` and filters title only. The store holds both refs (`external_ref` from the push, `issue_ref` from an accepted verdict, `skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:272`). So "why does DOW-3 exist?" has no lookup: the agent must list every card and guess by title. Fixed: `show` accepts an fp, an inbox ref (`DW-n`) or an issue key and resolves it, refusing an ambiguous match with the candidates; `list` returns the two refs when set. Lives in the proposal-model / triage-memory paths, so out of this round.

## Flow
- runner, new session: "why is DOW-3 in our backlog?"
- agent: `show DOW-3` -> exit 2, not found
- agent falls back to `list --title` on a guessed word
- fix: `show DOW-3` resolves through issue_ref, `show DW-3` through external_ref

## Expected impact
Ask-why works from the link people actually have. Could break: an fp that looks like a key (fps are hex; keys carry a dash) - pinned by a test.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - ask-why answers from a Jira key
Before: 0 of 2 non-fp handles resolve (show exits 2)
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked show and list against the schema; the case test is the instrument a worker writes first
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The installer reports success but never says what to do next
impact_why: a first-time user gets a JSON plan and no "open a project and type /dowser" or connect step
instrument: install.test.mjs case: installed output carries `next` for claude and codex (0 of 2 today)
evidence:
skill/install.mjs:282-284: "if (opts.scope === 'project') { notes.push('project scope writes into the current folder; ..."
skill/install.mjs:337: "process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ installed: true, ...plan }, null, 2) + '\n');"
body:
## Summary
`skill/install.mjs:337` prints `{installed: true, ...plan}`; `notes` is set only for project scope, so the output never names the first step (restart the assistant in a project, type /dowser, or in Codex "use the dowser skill") or the optional Jira connection.

## Description
README carries the next steps (`README.md:48-53`), but a user who ran the one-liner sees only paths and a stamp. Fixed: the result gains `next`, two or three lines per harness: start a new session in a project folder and type `/dowser` (Codex: ask for "the dowser skill"); to connect Jira, `claude mcp add --transport http dowser <url>` per docs/forge-app.md; a linked dev install says edits apply immediately.

## Flow
- user runs `node skill/install.mjs --harness codex`
- output: JSON with source, target, items, stamp
- user does not know Codex needs a new session or the phrasing
- fix: `next` lines in the output

## Expected impact
Fewer stalls between install and first scan. Could break: consumers parsing the JSON see one more key (additive).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - steps to first success shown after install
Before: 0 of 2 harness outputs carry a next step
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked both harness outputs; the test is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Shared scan markdown carries no link back to the inbox cards
impact_why: a team reading the shared doc cannot click through to triage the pushed card
instrument: share.test.mjs case: a pushed card's section links its external_url (0 of 1 today)
body:
## Summary
`share --run` (SKILL.md section 9 step 4) renders each card with its evidence refs only (`skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:20-22`); a pushed card's inbox link (`external_url`) and an accepted card's Jira issue are left out.

## Description
The shared markdown is the one Dowser output that travels beyond the runner (a doc, a slide). Every reader of it who wants to act must find the card in the inbox by title. The store has `external_url` and `issue_url` on pushed / accepted cards (`skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:272`). Fixed: a card heading line ends with `[DW-n](<external_url>)` when pushed, `[<issue_ref>](<issue_url>)` when accepted; no link when local only.

## Flow
- runner: "share this run as markdown"
- share prints titles, facts, evidence refs
- reader in Confluence cannot open the card
- fix: per-card link to the inbox or the issue

## Expected impact
Shared reports drive readers into the inbox, where decisions happen. Could break: nothing; additive markdown.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a shared card links to where it is decided
Before: 0 of N pushed cards linked
After: N of N (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked cardMd; share.mjs is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Headless runs never push, so a scheduled scan cannot feed the Jira inbox
impact_why: the plan's weeks 3-4 "scheduled scans" deliver nothing to the inbox where triage happens
evidence:
skill/SKILL.md:464: "else from section 7: no dialog, no `rules offer`, no `move` by `human:` - \"keep the rest\" is"
skill/SKILL.md:465: "the default for every card. Skip section 8: nothing is pushed."
docs/concepts/project-status-and-next-steps.md:195: "weeks 1-2: production path and judge path; 3-4: real-repo quality, scheduled"
body:
## Summary
SKILL.md section 11 step 3 skips the push on every headless run, so `claude -p` on a schedule or in CI leaves its cards on the machine that ran it.

## Description
Headless "runs the same pipeline up to the point where a person would decide" and then "Skip section 8: nothing is pushed" (`skill/SKILL.md:464`). But the person decides in the Jira inbox, not only in the local pre-triage: a pushed card is still undecided until someone clicks there (`skill/SKILL.md:406-407`). The project plan names scheduled scans for weeks 3-4 (`docs/concepts/project-status-and-next-steps.md:195`); a CI runner's `~/.dowser` is thrown away with the job, so under today's rule a scheduled scan produces nothing anyone sees. Option: an opt-in `push: yes` argument (or a stored pref) that lets a headless connected run push verified cards marked "not pre-triaged locally", leaving the local dialog the only thing skipped. That changes who the first reader is, so it is a product call.

## Flow
- CI job: `claude -p "/dowser mode: dev"` nightly, connected
- lenses, verify, pretriage run; push skipped by section 11
- job ends, its home folder is discarded: 0 cards reach the inbox
- option: `push: yes` -> section 8 runs, cards land marked as unreviewed

## Expected impact
Scheduled scans become a feed for the inbox; the person still decides every card in Jira. Could break: an unattended run filling an inbox with unfiltered cards; the opt-in and the budget of 16 bound it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a scheduled scan delivers its cards to the inbox
Before: headless connected run: 0 cards pushed (section 11 step 3)
After: with the opt-in: verified cards pushed, marked as not pre-triaged locally (predicted, not measured)
Method: simulation - walked the CI flow through sections 8 and 11; a probe needs a connected headless run, an operator act
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: The first full scan sets no expectation of scope or length
impact_why: a first-time runner gets no "reading the whole project, later scans are faster" line; only the fallback case is announced
instrument: procedure test asserting section 4 names a first-run line (dev and guided)
evidence:
skill/SKILL.md:153: "- `full` when no run has finished yet, or when the last full run is 14 or more days old."
skill/SKILL.md:167: "a full scan takes longer (guided: \"Dowser will read the whole project this time, because the"
body:
## Summary
SKILL.md section 4 step 2 tells the runner a full scan takes longer only after a `fallback`; the very first run, which is always `full` (`skill/SKILL.md:153`), starts the lenses silently.

## Description
The fallback wording ("Dowser will read the whole project this time...", `skill/SKILL.md:167`) is exactly what a first-time runner needs and does not get. Fixed: when `status` shows no finished run, say once before the first lens: dev "full scan (first run): every file; later runs read what changed"; guided "This is Dowser's first look at the project, so it reads all of it. Later scans only read what changed."

## Flow
- new user types /dowser
- preflight, run start mode full
- lenses start; no line about why it is slow this time
- fix: one first-run line before the lenses

## Expected impact
First-run patience and a correct mental model of incremental scans. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the first run states its scope
Before: 0 of 2 modes say anything on a first full run
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked section 4 for a fresh store
Result: better
Gate: none

title: No uninstall path for the skill
impact_why: removing Dowser means finding the per-harness folder by hand
instrument: install.test.mjs case: --uninstall removes a copy and a link, refuses a non-Dowser folder
body:
## Summary
`skill/install.mjs` installs, links and checks, but has no `--uninstall`; README documents none.

## Description
The four target folders differ per harness and scope (`skill/install.mjs:8-12`). `removeInstall` already exists with the right guards (`isDowserInstall`, unlink-not-follow for links). Fixed: `--uninstall --harness <h> [--scope]` reuses them, leaves `~/.dowser` (memory) in place and says so.

Registry technique: software-engineering/packaging installer-authoring ("Uninstall - the reaper, designed at creation time"; "everything written names its remover"). install.json now enumerates the installed files (2a1de4a), so uninstall can remove exactly that enumeration and leave ~/.dowser alone.

## Flow
- user wants Dowser gone
- no command; they search for ~/.claude/skills/dowser or ~/.codex/skills/dowser
- fix: --uninstall

## Expected impact
Clean exit for trial users. Could break: a guard regression would delete a non-Dowser folder; the existing guard is reused.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - removal in one command
Before: 0 commands
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked install.mjs
Result: better
Gate: none
